findings.body_chart: Pain in one small spot at the very bottom of the spine, between the buttocks.
findings.pain_behaviour: Worse sitting on hard chairs, leaning back and standing up from sitting. Better leaning forward or standing.
findings.palpation: Very tender right on the tip of the coccyx.
findings.red_flags: No weight loss, fever, night pain or bladder or bowel changes. No lump or discharge.
findings.rom_lumbar: Full and doesn't bring on the pain.
findings.neuro_symptoms: None.
findings.goals: I want to sit through a work meeting.

name: Jodie
situation: Jodie, 31, had a baby five months ago and wants to start running again. She can walk comfortably, but jumping brings on pressure and leaks.
diagnosis: Pelvic floor symptoms with impact, not ready to return to running yet
story: Jodie copes with walking and step-downs, but repeated hopping brings on vaginal pressure and leaking. Her pelvic floor isn't ready for running impact yet, so she needs graded pelvic floor and impact training before a return to run.

findings.hpc: Walking is fine, but when I tried a few jumps with the kids I felt pressure and leaked.
findings.hop_squat: After 12 single-leg hops she feels pressure and leaks. Step-downs and squats are fine.
findings.questionnaire: Leaks only with jumping and running. No urgency.
findings.cough_test: With consent, the pelvic floor contraction is fair but tires after 5 seconds.
findings.standing_balance: Steady on one leg for 30 seconds.
findings.medical_notes: Vaginal birth five months ago, small tear.
findings.mmt: Glutes and calves have good strength.
findings.goals: I want to run 5 km.

name: Ravi
situation: Ravi, 56, has been referred to the dizziness clinic. For a week the room has spun for a few seconds every time he rolls onto his right side in bed.
story: Ravi's vertigo lasts seconds and comes with rolling right and looking up. The right Dix-Hallpike brings on brief upbeating torsional nystagmus, which is right posterior canal BPPV, treated with the Epley manoeuvre.

findings.hpc: When I roll onto my right side in bed, the room spins for a few seconds. It also happens when I look up to a high shelf.
findings.dizziness: Proper spinning, like the room's turning, but only for a few seconds and only when I move my head a certain way.
findings.positional_test: Right Dix-Hallpike brings on spinning after a short delay, with upbeating torsional nystagmus that fades within 30 seconds. Left side is negative.
findings.vestibular_ocular: Head impulse test is normal both ways.
findings.cranial_nerves: Normal. No double vision, slurred speech or weakness.
findings.standing_balance: Steady.
findings.red_flags: No hearing loss or ringing.
findings.goals: I want to sleep on my right side again.

name: Leanne
situation: Leanne, 63, has been referred to the dizziness clinic. The room spins briefly when she rolls over in bed either way, worse rolling left.
story: Leanne's supine roll test brings on horizontal nystagmus beating towards the ground on both sides, stronger to the left. That's left horizontal canal BPPV, which needs a different repositioning manoeuvre than the posterior canal type.

findings.hpc: When I roll over in bed the room spins for a bit. It happens both ways, but rolling left is worse.
findings.dizziness: The room spins for under a minute when I roll over in bed, then it settles.
findings.positional_test: Dix-Hallpike gives no torsional nystagmus. The supine roll test brings on horizontal nystagmus beating towards the ground on both sides, stronger when turned to the left.
findings.cranial_nerves: Normal. No double vision or speech changes.
findings.red_flags: No new headache, weakness or hearing change.
findings.standing_balance: Steady.
findings.goals: I just want the spinning to stop.

name: Tariq
situation: Tariq, 50, had a bad bout of spinning vertigo two months ago that kept him in bed for days. He's better, but quick head turns still make things blur and he feels unsteady.
story: After vestibular neuritis Tariq's right inner ear isn't fully working. A head impulse to the right shows a catch-up saccade, and his vision blurs with quick head movement. Gaze stability exercises and balance training are the plan.

findings.hpc: Two months ago I had spinning that kept me in bed for three days. That's gone, but if I turn my head quickly things blur and I feel off.
findings.vestibular_ocular: Head impulse to the right shows a catch-up saccade. Dynamic visual acuity drops four lines when his head moves.
findings.standing_balance: Sways a lot standing on foam with his eyes closed.
findings.dizziness: It doesn't spin any more. I just feel off balance if I move my head quickly.
findings.gait: Veers when turning his head while walking.
findings.goals: I want to drive and play tennis again.

name: Maja
situation: Maja, 32, has had episodes of dizziness for a year. She's had migraines since she was a teenager.
diagnosis: Possible vestibular migraine (needs a medical diagnosis)
story: Maja's dizzy spells last hours and come with light and sound sensitivity, often alongside her migraine headaches. Positional testing and the inner ear checks are normal. That points to vestibular migraine, which needs a medical diagnosis and migraine management.

findings.hpc: The dizzy spells last a few hours. Lights and sounds feel really intense during them, and some come with my usual headaches.
findings.dizziness: Episodes last 1 to 6 hours, about twice a month. Swaying and spinning.
findings.associated: Light and sound sensitivity and nausea during episodes. Often around her period and after poor sleep.
findings.positional_test: Dix-Hallpike and roll tests are negative.
findings.red_flags: No hearing loss, double vision, weakness or sudden severe headache.
findings.goals: I want to stop missing work.

name: Thandi
situation: Thandi, 43, had an inner ear problem a year ago that got better. But most days she still feels like the floor is moving, especially in supermarkets and crowds.
story: Thandi's original inner ear problem has healed, but she's had non-spinning dizziness most days for months, worse upright and in visually busy places. Clinical tests are normal. That fits persistent postural-perceptual dizziness, treated with habituation exercises and graded exposure.

findings.hpc: Most days I feel like the floor's unstable, like being on a boat. Supermarket aisles and crowds are the worst.
findings.dizziness: It's not spinning. It's a rocking, swaying feeling most days for the last nine months. It's worse when I'm standing or walking and better lying down.
findings.vestibular_ocular: Head impulse is normal both ways. Watching moving stripes makes her feel worse.
findings.questionnaire: High score on a dizziness handicap questionnaire. Anxiety about going out.
findings.standing_balance: Holds herself stiffly, but her balance tests are within normal limits.
findings.goals: I want to do my grocery shopping.

name: Arthur
situation: Arthur, 75, has been referred to the balance clinic. Things bounce when he walks and his balance is much worse in dim light.
story: Arthur had a course of strong IV antibiotics last year. Both head impulse directions show catch-up saccades, his vision bounces with walking and he relies on vision for balance. That's possible bilateral vestibular loss, which needs specialist confirmation and balance and gaze training.

findings.hpc: When I walk, the world bounces up and down so I can't read signs. In the dark I'm all over the place.
findings.vestibular_ocular: Head impulses to both sides show catch-up saccades. Dynamic visual acuity drops five lines.
findings.standing_balance: Steady with his eyes open on a firm floor. Falls on foam with his eyes closed.
findings.meds: Had a long course of gentamicin for an infection last year.
findings.coordination: Normal finger to nose and heel to shin.
findings.falls_history: Fell in the garden at dusk.
findings.goals: I want to walk safely at night.

name: Julia
situation: Julia, 48, works long hours at a computer. She gets a headache on one side that starts near the back of her neck.
story: Julia's one-sided headache starts at the neck, comes on after long sessions at the desk and is reproduced by pressure on her upper neck joints. Her neck rotation is limited. That fits cervicogenic headache, once red flags are excluded.

findings.hpc: It starts at the back of my neck on the right and spreads over my head to behind my eye, usually after long days at the computer.
findings.red_flags: No sudden worst-ever headache, fever, neuro changes, visual loss or jaw pain on chewing.
findings.rom_cervical: Flexion-rotation test is limited to 25 degrees on the right and brings on her headache.
findings.paivm: Pressing on the right C1 to C2 joint reproduces her familiar headache.
findings.dnf: Deep neck flexor endurance is 12 seconds.
findings.neuro_symptoms: None.
findings.body_chart: Pain on the right side of the neck spreading to behind the right eye. Always the same side.
findings.goals: I want to work a full day without a headache.

name: Sami
situation: Sami, 59, has walked in with severe dizziness that hasn't stopped since this morning. He's seeing double and struggling to stand.
diagnosis: Possible posterior circulation stroke. Emergency escalation
story: Continuous vertigo with new double vision, a normal head impulse, nystagmus that changes direction and not being able to sit or stand without help are central warning signs. That's a possible posterior circulation stroke, so call an ambulance now.

findings.hpc: It started this morning and hasn't stopped. I'm seeing double and I can't stand without holding on.
findings.cranial_nerves: New double vision on looking to the left. Slightly slurred speech.
findings.vestibular_ocular: Head impulse is normal both ways. Nystagmus changes direction with gaze. Skew deviation on cover test.
findings.red_flags: I've got high blood pressure and I smoke. It came on all of a sudden this morning.
findings.coordination: Clumsy finger to nose on the left.
findings.positional_test: Not appropriate. These signs need emergency care.
findings.dizziness: It hasn't stopped all day, whether I move my head or not.

name: Tess
situation: Tess, 27, had a concussion a month ago and is struggling to read. Screens and busy places bring on dizziness and headaches.
diagnosis: Visual and vestibular symptoms after concussion
story: A month after concussion, eye tracking, near focusing and visual motion all bring on Tess's symptoms, and their near point of convergence is far out. That's a visual-vestibular problem after concussion, treated with graded oculomotor and vestibular exercises.

findings.hpc: I can't read for long, and screens or busy shopping centres make me dizzy and give me a headache.
findings.vestibular_ocular: Smooth pursuits and saccades bring on headache and dizziness. Near point of convergence is 14 cm. Head turns while looking at a target make it worse.
findings.dizziness: A floating feeling with screens and busy places.
findings.red_flags: No worsening headache, vomiting or weakness.
findings.goals: I want to get back to study.

name: Anita
situation: Anita, 68, has had spinning attacks that last hours. Her left ear feels full, rings and her hearing comes and goes.
diagnosis: Possible Ménière's disease. Refer for diagnostic assessment
story: Anita has episodes of spinning lasting hours, along with fullness, ringing and fluctuating hearing in the left ear. Between attacks her positional tests are normal. That pattern fits Ménière's disease, which needs ENT and audiology assessment to confirm.

findings.hpc: The attacks of spinning last a couple of hours. Before one, my left ear feels full and rings, and my hearing goes muffled.
findings.dizziness: The room spins for two to four hours and I'm vomiting. It happens every few weeks.
findings.associated: Ringing, fullness and fluctuating low hearing in the left ear before and during attacks.
findings.positional_test: Dix-Hallpike and roll tests negative between attacks.
findings.imaging: An audiogram is needed. MRI may be ordered to rule out other causes.
findings.cranial_nerves: Normal apart from reduced hearing on the left.
findings.goals: I want to stop the attacks.

name: Darren
situation: Darren, 40, works in a warehouse and has been off for six weeks with his back. He's planning to go back but he's nervous about lifting stock all day.
diagnosis: Work limited by fear and low lifting tolerance after back pain (graded return to work)
story: Darren's back has settled and his neuro screen is clear. Light lifts are fine, but his worry climbs and his lifting stiffens as the repetitions build. A graded return to work with lifting practice, and a plan worked out with his employer, is the answer.

findings.hpc: Walking's fine now. I just don't trust my back with lifting boxes all shift, over and over.
findings.beliefs: Thinks bending will 'put his disc out' again. Worry goes up with each lift.
findings.questionnaire: High score on a fear-avoidance questionnaire for work.
findings.hop_squat: Lifts a 10 kg box from the floor five times comfortably. By 15 he's holding his breath and keeping his back rigid.
findings.red_flags: No red flags.
findings.neuro_symptoms: None.
findings.rom_lumbar: Full, a little guarded on bending.
findings.social: Job involves lifting up to 15 kg repeatedly for eight hours.
findings.goals: I want to get back to full shifts.

name: Gabriela
situation: Gabriela, 34, is a hairdresser. Her right hand tingles at night, and shaking it helps.
story: Gabriela's tingling is in her thumb and first two fingers, worst at night and eased by shaking her hand. Phalen's and Tinel's at the wrist reproduce it and the neck is clear. That's carpal tunnel syndrome, often managed first with a night splint and changes to how she works.

findings.hpc: My hand goes numb and tingly at night and wakes me up. I shake it and it gets better. Holding scissors all day makes it worse too.
findings.body_chart: Tingling in the right thumb, index and middle fingers. The little finger is fine.
findings.carpal_tunnel: Phalen's brings on her tingling in 30 seconds. Tinel's over the carpal tunnel is positive.
findings.dermatomes: Light touch is slightly reduced on the thumb side of the palm and the first three fingers.
findings.grip: Pinch strength slightly weaker on the right.
findings.observation: No wasting at the base of the thumb.
findings.rom_cervical: Full and doesn't change the hand symptoms.
findings.goals: I want to sleep through and cut hair all day.

name: Kofi
situation: Kofi, 47, uses a wheelchair and drives for work. His shoulders have started aching after he gets in and out of the car many times a day.
story: Kofi does around 20 car transfers a day, pushing his whole body weight through his arms each time. His shoulders ache with the repeated load, and push-up transfers reproduce it. Changing his car and transfer setup and strengthening his shoulders are the plan.

findings.hpc: I'm in and out of the car about 20 times a day. By the afternoon both shoulders ache, the right more.
findings.social: Paraplegic for 15 years. Lifts his wheelchair into the car himself.
findings.cuff_tests: Resisted external rotation and empty can reproduce the ache, slightly weak on the right.
findings.painful_arc: Painful between 80 and 120 degrees on the right.
findings.observation: Push-up transfer to the car seat brings on his shoulder pain.
findings.goals: I want to keep driving for work without pain.

name: Elif
situation: Elif, 28, is a violinist who's practising longer for an audition. Her left forearm aches while she plays, but it's better on days off.
story: Elif doubled her daily practice, with long static holds and repetitive fingering. Her forearm muscles are overloaded, which brings on the ache, and it settles with rest. There are no nerve signs. Graded practice time, breaks and strengthening are the plan.

findings.hpc: I'm practising five hours a day for an audition. My forearm aches while I play and it's better on days off.
findings.social: Went from two to five hours of practice a day in three weeks. No breaks.
findings.palpation: Diffuse tenderness through the forearm flexor muscles. No single tender spot.
findings.mmt: Sustained resisted finger flexion brings on the familiar ache after 40 seconds.
findings.neuro_symptoms: No pins and needles or numbness.
findings.elbow_tendon: Resisted wrist movements aren't painful at the elbow tendons.
findings.goals: I want to play well for the audition.

name: Mackenzie
situation: Mackenzie, 23, is a hospital orderly coming back to work after a back strain. They lose confidence when they have to move patients they don't know.
diagnosis: Needs graded manual handling practice to return to work
story: Mackenzie's back has recovered, but unfamiliar patients shake their confidence. With a slide sheet and clear talking with the patient, their technique and confidence improve. Graded handling practice before full duties is the plan.

findings.hpc: With patients I know I'm fine, but when it's someone new I freeze up and worry I'll hurt my back again.
findings.observation: With a slide sheet and talking the patient through it, their technique is smooth. Without them they rush and twist.
findings.beliefs: Worried about reinjury, mostly with heavier or confused patients.
findings.red_flags: No red flags. Back strain has settled.
findings.neuro_symptoms: None.
findings.goals: I want to go back to full shifts on the wards.

name: Bao
situation: Bao, 61, had his leg amputated below the knee two years ago. He's walking less because his leg has started moving around in his prosthesis.
diagnosis: Poorly fitting prosthetic socket limiting walking
story: Bao has lost weight and his residual limb has shrunk, so it pistons up and down in the socket and rubs. That's a socket fit problem. Adding socks helps for now, but he needs his prosthetist to adjust or remake the socket.

findings.hpc: Since my leg started slipping around inside the prosthesis, I walk less because it rubs.
findings.gait: His limb visibly drops in the socket as he steps and he vaults over the prosthetic side.
findings.skin_wound: Red pressure marks below the kneecap and at the end of the limb. No open wounds.
findings.observation: Gap at the top of the socket. Wearing only one sock.
findings.social: Lost 8 kg in the past six months.
findings.pulses: Good pulses in the other foot.
findings.goals: I want to walk to the temple again.

name: Marlene
situation: Marlene, 57, lives on a farm two hours from town. She wants to get her shoulder working again after surgery, but she can't get to weekly appointments.
diagnosis: Can't access weekly rehab in person. Suits a hybrid plan with telehealth
story: Marlene's shoulder rehab is on track, but transport is the barrier. She has reliable video on her phone and safe space at home, so a hybrid plan with occasional in-person visits and video check-ins in between works.

findings.hpc: I want to get my shoulder going again, but it's two hours each way to town and I can't drive yet.
findings.social: Lives on a farm two hours from the clinic. Reliable phone video. Space at home to exercise. Her husband can drive her once a month.
findings.medical_notes: Rotator cuff repair eight weeks ago. Recovery on track.
findings.cuff_tests: Not tested yet, too early after the repair.
findings.goals: I want to hang washing and help on the farm.

name: Nasir
situation: Nasir, 38, is a mechanic who uses power tools all day. His fingers go white in the cold and numb after long jobs with the rattle gun.
diagnosis: Possible hand-arm vibration syndrome. Refer to occupational health
story: After 15 years of using vibrating tools, Nasir's fingers blanch in the cold and go numb after long tool use. That fits hand-arm vibration syndrome, which needs an occupational health referral and less exposure to vibration.

findings.hpc: My fingertips go white and numb when it's cold, and after a long day on the rattle gun my hands ache and tingle.
findings.observation: Photos he took show the ends of his fingers going white, then blue, then red.
findings.dermatomes: Reduced sensation at all his fingertips on both hands.
findings.social: Uses impact wrenches and grinders for five or six hours a day, for 15 years.
findings.grip: Slightly reduced grip on both sides.
findings.goals: I want to keep working as a mechanic.

name: Sharon
situation: Sharon, 52, has long-term pain and started using a walking stick a few months ago. Since then her right wrist has been sore.
diagnosis: Wrist overload from the walking stick
story: Sharon leans heavily through a straight-handled cane set too low, which forces her wrist into extension. Her wrist pain eases when the handle height is adjusted and an ergonomic handle is used.

findings.hpc: My right wrist has hurt ever since I started leaning on my walking stick.
findings.walking_aid: Her cane is 6 cm too short. With the right height and a moulded handle, her wrist pain drops from 6 to 2.
findings.rom_wrist: Full, but extension with weight through her hand hurts.
findings.palpation: Tender over the back of the wrist.
findings.gait: Leans heavily on the cane, wrist bent back.
findings.goals: I want to keep walking with the stick without wrist pain.

name: Piet
situation: Piet, 46, burnt the back of his right hand at work three months ago and wants to go back. The skin feels tight and he struggles to grip and get gloves on.
diagnosis: Scar tightness limiting hand movement after the burn
story: Piet's healed burn scar across the back of his hand is tight and raised, which limits how far his fingers bend. Scar massage, stretching, pressure garments and grip work are the plan.

findings.hpc: The skin on the back of my hand is so tight I can't make a full fist or get my work gloves on.
findings.skin_wound: Raised, red, firm scar across the back of the hand. It blanches and pulls tight when he makes a fist.
findings.rom_wrist: Can't fully bend his fingers. The fingertips stay 3 cm from his palm.
findings.grip: Grip 22 kg on the right against 45 on the left.
findings.observation: The skin stretches white over his knuckles when he bends his fingers.
findings.goals: I want to go back to my factory job.

name: Amal
situation: Amal, 42, is an accounts manager. Her lower back has been sore on and off for two years, and it's starting to affect her work and sleep.
diagnosis: Persistent low back pain with fear avoidance
answers: persistent low back pain with fear
chronic low back pain with fear
story: Amal's back has been sore for two years without any sign of something serious. Each flare convinces her she's done new damage, so she braces, avoids bending and has stopped the gym. Her movement is guarded but eases as she practises, and her questionnaire shows high fear of movement. Building confidence with graded exposure matters as much as the exercises.

findings.hpc: It's been two years now. Some days it's fine, then out of nowhere it flares and I'm sure I've done something to it again. I've stopped going to the gym and I don't sleep well.
findings.body_chart: Across my lower back, sometimes into my right buttock. Nothing down my legs.
findings.pain_score: About a 3 most days, up to an 8 when it flares.
findings.pain_behaviour: Bending to load the dishwasher, sitting through long meetings. Moving around and a hot shower help.
findings.pain_24h: I wake up two or three times a night when I roll over.
findings.red_flags: No weight loss, fevers, night sweats, cancer or bladder or bowel changes.
findings.neuro_symptoms: No pins and needles or numbness.
findings.previous_episodes: It's flared about six times in the last two years.
findings.beliefs: I'm scared bending will slip a disc. My scan said I've got a bulge and wear and tear, so I try to keep my back straight all the time.
findings.imaging: An MRI from last year shows mild disc bulges at two levels, which are common at her age without pain.
findings.questionnaire: High score on the fear of movement questionnaire. Moderate disability on the back pain questionnaire.
findings.rom_lumbar: Bends slowly with a stiff, braced back and holds her breath, reaching just past her knees. With some coaching and a few repetitions she reaches mid-shin with less pain.
findings.goals: I want to get back to the gym and sleep through the night.

name: Rebecca
situation: Rebecca, 49, is a school librarian. She's been sore all over for over a year, sleeps badly and feels exhausted most days.
diagnosis: Widespread pain pattern. Needs a medical assessment for fibromyalgia
story: Rebecca's pain moves around both sides of her body, above and below the waist, and has gone on for more than a year. She sleeps poorly, wakes unrefreshed and has foggy days. Her joints aren't swollen and her blood tests are normal. That pattern fits fibromyalgia, which her GP diagnoses. Physio helps with paced, gentle activity that builds up slowly.

findings.hpc: It moves around. One week it's my neck and shoulders, the next it's my hips and legs. I'm tired all the time, and a normal day at work leaves me flat for the evening.
findings.body_chart: Both sides, above and below my waist. Neck, shoulders, upper and lower back, hips and thighs.
findings.pain_score: About a 5 most days, worse after a busy day.
findings.pain_behaviour: Busy days, stress and bad sleep make it worse. A warm bath and gentle walks help a bit.
findings.pain_24h: I sleep badly and wake up feeling like I haven't slept. Mornings are stiff.
findings.red_flags: No weight loss, fever or rashes.
findings.associated: Some days my head's foggy and I lose my words. My gut plays up too.
findings.palpation: Tender to light pressure in lots of places on both sides of her body.
findings.observation: No joint swelling, redness or deformity.
findings.bloods: Her GP's blood tests, including inflammation markers and thyroid, are normal.
findings.exercise_tolerance: Manages 10 minutes of walking comfortably. Longer walks leave her sore and tired the next day.
findings.rom_cervical: Full range with some discomfort at the end.
findings.goals: I want to get through a work week without needing the weekend to recover.

name: Benjamin
situation: Benjamin, 66, finished treatment for breast cancer on his right side last year. His right arm feels heavier and his shirt sleeves have got tighter on that side.
diagnosis: Possible cancer-related upper limb lymphoedema. Refer for lymphoedema assessment
story: Benjamin had lymph nodes removed from under his right arm and radiotherapy last year. Over the past few months his right arm has slowly got fuller and heavier, with no redness, heat or fever. The measurements are clearly bigger on that side. That points to lymphoedema, which needs a specialist lymphoedema assessment and compression and exercise advice, once infection and a clot are ruled out.

findings.hpc: Over the last few months my right arm's felt heavier, like it's full. My shirt cuff and my watch are tighter on that side.
findings.body_chart: The whole right arm feels heavy and achy, more in the forearm.
findings.pain_score: Not really pain, just a heavy ache. About a 2.
findings.pmhx: Breast cancer on the right last year. Had surgery with lymph nodes taken out from under my arm, then radiotherapy.
findings.red_flags: No fevers, no redness, no hot patches. It came on slowly, not overnight.
findings.swelling: Arm measurements are 2 to 3 cm bigger on the right at the forearm and upper arm. Pressing the skin leaves a slight dent.
findings.skin_wound: Skin is a normal colour and temperature. No redness, cuts or rash. The scar has healed well.
findings.observation: The right forearm and hand look fuller than the left.
findings.rom_shoulder: Slightly stiff going overhead on the right, otherwise full.
findings.dvt: No sudden onset, no pain in the arm veins or warmth. Low suspicion for a clot.
findings.goals: I want my arm to stop feeling so heavy so I can get back to woodwork.

name: Gita
situation: Gita, 61, is having chemotherapy for bowel cancer. She's so tired that walking to the letterbox and doing housework wipe her out.
story: Gita's chemotherapy has left her tired in a way rest doesn't fix, and she's done less and less, so her fitness has dropped too. Her blood counts are safe for exercise today and her vital signs are fine. Light walking feels hard for her. A gentle, monitored programme that fits around her treatment cycle is the plan, and exercise actually helps cancer-related fatigue.

findings.hpc: I'm halfway through my chemo. I'm tired in a way sleep doesn't fix. Walking to the letterbox or hanging out one load of washing and I need to sit down.
findings.pmhx: Bowel cancer. Surgery in March, now on chemotherapy every two weeks.
findings.prior_function: I used to walk 5 km with my sister every morning.
findings.bloods: Today's blood counts and platelets are within the safe range for exercise. Her haemoglobin is a little low but stable.
findings.obs: Heart rate 84, blood pressure 118/74, oxygen saturation 98%, temperature normal.
findings.exercise_tolerance: After four minutes of easy walking she rates it as hard. Heart rate goes up to 112.
findings.six_mwt: Walks 330 metres in six minutes, well below what's expected for her age, with one rest.
findings.sit_to_stand: Five sit to stands take 15 seconds.
findings.beliefs: I thought I was supposed to rest during chemo.
findings.goals: I want to walk to the park with my grandson.

name: Ian
situation: Ian, 72, has prostate cancer. He's come in with new back pain and says his legs are getting weaker.
diagnosis: Suspected metastatic spinal cord compression. Emergency escalation
story: Ian has prostate cancer, new severe back pain that's worst at night, and legs that have got weaker and clumsier over a week, with brisk reflexes and some numbness. That's suspected metastatic spinal cord compression. It's an emergency: he needs urgent medical review and an MRI today, not a home exercise programme.

findings.hpc: My back started hurting about three weeks ago, but in the last week it's got really bad, worse at night, and my legs feel weak and wobbly. I nearly fell on the step this morning.
findings.body_chart: Middle of my back, with a band of pain around my ribs on both sides.
findings.pain_score: 8 out of 10, and nothing touches it at night.
findings.pain_24h: It's worst lying down at night. I've been sleeping in the recliner.
findings.red_flags: Prostate cancer diagnosed two years ago. I've lost 5 kg without trying.
findings.cauda_equina: I've had to rush to the toilet a couple of times this week. No numbness around my bottom.
findings.neuro_symptoms: My feet feel numb and like they're not mine.
findings.myotomes: Both legs are weak, hip flexion and ankle dorsiflexion 4-/5 on both sides.
findings.reflexes: Knee and ankle reflexes are brisk on both sides.
findings.umn: Both big toes go up when the sole is stroked. A few beats of ankle clonus.
findings.dermatomes: Reduced feeling from the chest down on both sides.
findings.gait: Wide-based and unsteady. Needs a hand to walk.
findings.goals: I just want the pain sorted.

name: Lucía
situation: Lucía, 35, is a graphic designer. Her joints often feel like they slip out of place, and some days she's far more tired and sore than others.
diagnosis: Symptomatic generalised joint hypermobility. Assess for an underlying condition
story: Lucía's joints move well beyond the usual range in many places, and her shoulders and kneecaps feel like they slip. She bruises easily, gets tired and her symptoms vary day to day. That fits symptomatic generalised hypermobility, and she should be assessed for an underlying condition such as hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome. Strength and control work, paced activity and joint protection are the focus.

findings.hpc: My shoulders and kneecaps feel like they slip out and back in. Some days I'm fine, other days everything aches and I'm exhausted after work.
findings.body_chart: Both shoulders, both knees, sometimes my wrists from the mouse.
findings.pain_score: Anywhere from 2 to 7, depending on the day.
findings.pain_behaviour: Carrying shopping, yoga poses that hang on my joints, long days at the desk.
findings.previous_episodes: I've had my right kneecap pop out twice as a teenager.
findings.associated: I bruise really easily and I always get dizzy if I stand up too fast.
findings.observation: Elbows and knees go back past straight. She can put her palms flat on the floor with straight knees and bend her thumb to her forearm. Beighton score 7 out of 9.
findings.rom_elbow: Both elbows go 15 degrees past straight.
findings.rom_knee: Both knees go 10 degrees past straight.
findings.instability: Right shoulder feels like it'll slip with the arm out to the side and rotated back.
findings.patellofemoral: Kneecaps move more than usual side to side, and the right one makes her nervous when pushed outwards.
findings.goals: I want to work and go to the gym without paying for it for days.

name: Greg
situation: Greg, 58, broke his right wrist eight weeks ago. The bone has healed, but his hand burns and even light touch hurts.
diagnosis: Possible complex regional pain syndrome. Needs specialist assessment
story: Greg's wrist fracture has healed, but his hand is swollen, burning, sweatier and warmer than the other one, and light touch is painful. Those changes are well beyond normal recovery. With no other cause found, that fits complex regional pain syndrome, which needs early specialist assessment and gentle, graded use of the hand rather than protecting it.

findings.hpc: The cast came off a month ago and the X-ray says it's healed, but my hand burns all the time. Even my shirt cuff brushing it hurts, and it goes red and hot.
findings.body_chart: Burning through the whole right hand and wrist, not following any one finger.
findings.pain_behaviour: Anything touching it, cold air, trying to use it. I keep it tucked against my chest.
findings.neuro_symptoms: It burns and tingles all over the hand, not just in certain fingers.
findings.imaging: X-ray shows the fracture has healed in a good position.
findings.dermatomes: Light touch with a cotton bud is painful over the whole hand, not in a nerve pattern.
findings.skin_wound: Right hand is warmer, redder and sweatier than the left, and the skin looks shiny.
findings.swelling: Right hand and fingers are puffy. Rings don't fit.
findings.rom_wrist: Very stiff wrist and fingers. Can't make a full fist.
findings.carpal_tunnel: Tinel's and Phalen's don't bring on tingling in the thumb and first fingers. Hard to test with the pain.
findings.grip: Too painful to grip the dynamometer.
findings.goals: I want to use my hand again and get back to bowls.

name: Isha
situation: Isha, 41, has rheumatoid arthritis. Their knee has been stiff for a fortnight and a few other joints have started to swell.
diagnosis: Possible inflammatory arthritis flare. Coordinate a rheumatology review
story: Isha's morning stiffness has stretched past an hour, and their knee, wrists and some finger joints are warm and swollen. They've missed doses of their medication. That pattern means the arthritis is flaring, and it needs a prompt rheumatology review so the medication can be adjusted. Physio keeps them moving gently in the meantime.

findings.hpc: My right knee has been stiff for about two weeks. Now my wrists and a couple of knuckles are puffy too, and it takes me ages to get going in the morning.
findings.body_chart: Right knee, both wrists and the knuckles of my first two fingers on each hand.
findings.pain_behaviour: Worse after sitting still. Better once I get moving.
findings.pain_24h: It takes over an hour and a hot shower to loosen up each morning.
findings.meds: Methotrexate once a week, but I've missed a few doses because I felt sick.
findings.red_flags: No fever, and I don't feel unwell in myself.
findings.swelling: Right knee has a moderate effusion. Both wrists and several knuckles are puffy.
findings.palpation: The knee, wrists and knuckles are warm and tender. The joint line is spongy.
findings.rom_knee: Bends to 95 degrees and stops 10 degrees short of straight.
findings.bloods: Inflammation markers are up compared with last time.
findings.goals: I want to get back to my morning walks.

name: Michael
situation: Michael, 53, flew back from London four days ago. His left calf has been sore and swollen since.
diagnosis: Possible deep vein thrombosis. Urgent medical referral
story: After a long-haul flight Michael has one swollen, tender, warm calf with no injury. The calf measures bigger and he scores as likely on the Wells screen. That's a possible deep vein thrombosis, which needs same-day medical review and an ultrasound, and no massage or exercise of the leg until it's been cleared.

findings.hpc: I got back from London on Sunday. Since then my left calf has been tight and sore, and my sock's leaving a mark on that side. I didn't do anything to it.
findings.body_chart: Left calf, all the way round.
findings.pain_score: About a 4, worse when I walk.
findings.pain_behaviour: Walking and standing make it ache. Putting it up helps a bit.
findings.red_flags: I'm not short of breath and I've got no chest pain.
findings.pmhx: Nothing much. Knee arthroscopy five years ago.
findings.swelling: Left calf measures 3.5 cm bigger than the right. Pitting swelling around the ankle.
findings.palpation: Tender along the back of the calf. The leg feels warmer.
findings.dvt: Wells score likely: whole calf swollen, more than 3 cm difference, pitting on one side, tender along the deep veins, recent long travel.
findings.skin_wound: Mild redness, no cuts or insect bites.
findings.goals: I want to get back to running.

name: Chloe
situation: Chloe, 30, has been seeing a community physio for back pain after a fall. Today she says her back and both legs are much worse.
diagnosis: Possible cauda equina syndrome. Emergency escalation
story: Chloe's back pain has suddenly worsened with pain down both legs, numbness around her bottom when she wipes and trouble feeling when her bladder is full. That's possible cauda equina syndrome, a surgical emergency. She needs to go to the emergency department straight away for an urgent MRI.

findings.hpc: Since yesterday my back's got much worse and now it's going down both legs. I've also noticed something weird when I go to the loo.
findings.body_chart: Low back, down the backs of both legs to my feet.
findings.cauda_equina: It feels numb around my bottom when I wipe, and I can't tell properly when my bladder's full. I've had to strain to start weeing.
findings.neuro_symptoms: Pins and needles in both feet.
findings.red_flags: No fever or weight loss.
findings.dermatomes: Reduced light touch around the buttocks and the backs of both thighs.
findings.myotomes: Weak ankle plantarflexion on both sides.
findings.slr: Brings on pain down both legs at 40 degrees.
findings.goals: I want this to stop.
